# GENERATED FILE -- do not hand-edit. Built by backend/scripts/build_connector_catalogue.py
# from backend/data/connectors/dice/{profile,definitions}.json.

FLIGHT DATA -- one table, tb_flight_fact_report

WHAT THIS IS, AND WHEN IT WAS MEASURED. Everything below was read from 13 daily load files
covering 1 January 2026 to 7 September 2026. It says what those files held; it is not a promise
about what the table holds today, and no value list here is a closed set. 131 of the table's 408
columns are described -- the rest are outside the agreed working set and are not listed.

ONE ROW PER FLIGHT PER LOAD. The same flight is re-stated in later files as its actual times are
filled in, so ALWAYS collapse to one row per flight by keeping the highest LAST_UPDATE_DATE_TIME
for each AODB_AFTTAB_PK_URNO. Skip that and you over-report flight counts, and every average over
those rows is wrong in the same direction.

THE FILE'S DATE IS THE LOAD DATE, NOT THE FLIGHT DATE. These files are stamped 1 January 2026 to 7
September 2026, and the flights inside them are scheduled between August 2022 and October 2026: a
load date bounds neither end of the flights in it. To get flights in a date range, read the files
and then filter ROWS on SIBT_SOBT_TIME, the merged scheduled time, present on arrivals and
departures alike. Do NOT filter on SCHEDULED_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_SOBT -- it is the DEPARTURE time and
is null on every arrival row, so it silently drops half the traffic. SCHEDULED_IN_BLOCK_TIME_SIBT
has the mirror-image problem.

TRIM TEXT BEFORE GROUPING OR COMPARING. Some text columns hold the same value twice, once padded
with trailing spaces: AIRLINE_NAME carries 'AKASA AIR' and a second, space-padded copy of it as
two distinct values, so a plain GROUP BY shows that airline twice. 15 values across 6 of the
columns below are padded like that, and only 2 of those 6 list their values here -- for the rest
the padding is invisible in this block, so assume it rather than look for it. Some columns also
use an EMPTY STRING rather than null, which IS NOT NULL does not filter -- FLIGHT_NATURE_TTYP_DESC
is one, and FLIGHT_TYPE_FTYP holds a single space. Trim, and treat blank as missing.

Column names ending in a four-letter code follow the EUROCONTROL A-CDM convention, where the first
three letters name the milestone (AIBT in-block, AOBT off-block, ALDT landing, ATOT take-off, TOBT
target off-block) and the fourth is an attribute of it.

MEASURES -- BIAL's own KPI definitions. Prefer these over inventing arithmetic. When a request
names one of these, use the formula and the columns given here: they are the airport's
definitions, not ours. Every one still obeys the rules above -- collapse to one row per flight,
and filter dates on SIBT_SOBT_TIME.

Turnaround time = next AOBT - AIBT for the same registration; uses ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT, ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT, AIRCRAFT_REGN; target 90 min wide-body / 45 min narrow-body
Departure OTP = share of departures where AOBT <= SOBT + 15 min; uses ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT, SCHEDULED_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_SOBT, FOR_OTP; target > 85%
Arrival OTP = share of arrivals where AIBT <= SIBT + 15 min; uses ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT, SCHEDULED_IN_BLOCK_TIME_SIBT, FOR_OTP; target > 85%
Taxi-out time = ATOT - AOBT; uses ACTUAL_TAKEOFF_TIME_ATOT, ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT; target < 12 min
Taxi-in time = AIBT - ALDT; uses ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT, ACTUAL_LANDING_TIME_ALDT; target < 10 min
Average departure delay = AOBT - SOBT; uses ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT, SCHEDULED_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_SOBT; target < 15 min
Average arrival delay = AIBT - SIBT; uses ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT, SCHEDULED_IN_BLOCK_TIME_SIBT; target < 15 min
Gate occupancy / ground time = AOBT - AIBT; uses ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT, ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT; target minimise
Total aircraft movements = count of flights with FOR_ATM = 1, deduped on the flight key; uses FOR_ATM, AODB_AFTTAB_PK_URNO; target set daily by BIAL
Peak hour movements = group by hour of SIBT_SOBT_TIME, count FOR_ATM = 1, take the largest; uses SIBT_SOBT_TIME, FOR_ATM, AODB_AFTTAB_PK_URNO; target stay within declared capacity
Runway throughput = take-offs + landings per hour; uses ACTUAL_TAKEOFF_TIME_ATOT, ACTUAL_LANDING_TIME_ALDT, RUNWAY; target limited by runway capacity
Departure queue time = ATOT - AOBT; uses ACTUAL_TAKEOFF_TIME_ATOT, ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT; target minimise
Airborne time = ALDT - ATOT; uses ACTUAL_LANDING_TIME_ALDT, ACTUAL_TAKEOFF_TIME_ATOT; target varies by route
Flights exceeding turnaround SLA = count where turnaround > the target for the body type; uses TAT, AIRCRAFT_BODY_TYPE; target < 5%
Aircraft waiting for stand = AIBT - ALDT, flagged when unusually long; uses ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT, ACTUAL_LANDING_TIME_ALDT; target minimise
Passenger throughput = sum of passengers, domestic and international split; uses NO_OF_PAX_PAXT, TOTAL_DOM_PAX, TOTAL_INT_PAX, FOR_PAX; target set daily by BIAL

FOR_ATM, FOR_OTP and FOR_PAX are BIAL's own inclusion flags (0/1, never null). Filter on the
matching flag when computing movements, punctuality or passenger totals -- a flight with the flag
at 0 is deliberately outside that KPI's denominator.

TWO ASSUMPTIONS WE MADE, because their formulas name fields the table does not have:

  ATD -> ACTUAL_OFF_BLOCK_TIME_AOBT (their formula says ATD, which does not exist; off-block chosen over take-off)
  ATA -> ACTUAL_IN_BLOCK_TIME_AIBT (their formula says ATA, which does not exist; in-block chosen over landing)

CANNOT BE ANSWERED from this table -- say so rather than approximating:

  Flight cancellation rate -- the flight-status column held no value in any profiled row
  Flight diversion rate -- the diversion column held no value in any profiled row
  Airside operational incidents -- needs an Incident Management System, which is not connected
  Runway incursions -- needs a Safety System, which is not connected
  Stand utilisation -- needs 'available stand time', which the table does not carry
  Contact / remote stand utilisation -- needs the contact-vs-remote classification too
  Apron congestion index -- needs a count of available stands
  Stand conflict events -- derivable from stand and times, but the allocation rules are not here

HOW TO READ THE COLUMN LINES. One line per column, grouped by what it is about. A column with no
type in brackets holds text; otherwise its type is stated -- (timestamp), (integer), (decimal). A
`--` at the end of a line is what that column means.

A line reading `= 'A', 'B'` lists the values that were present when this metadata was built. THAT
IS NOT A CLOSED SET: derive filter and dropdown values from the data at runtime rather than
hard-coding these, or the day a new code appears your app silently drops those rows. A line
reading `= at least N distinct values observed` means there were too many to list -- read them
from the data with SELECT DISTINCT at runtime.

## punctuality -- On-time performance and turnaround
FB_ONTIME (integer)

FOR_OTP (integer)
LB_ONTIME (integer)
OTP (integer) -- On-time performance for this flight, against schedule. SIGNED - negative is early, positive is late. The unit is SECONDS, not minutes: every one of the 301 values profiled is a whole multiple of 60, as are both extremes, which a minute-granular column would not be (TAT, a real minutes column, takes values like 9, 11 and 23). Divide by 60 before showing minutes. Observed range is roughly -90,720 to 253,860 - about -25 to +70 hours - so the extremes are data-quality outliers rather than real delays.
TAT (integer) -- Turnaround time in minutes - the interval between arrival on-stand and departure off-stand for the same aircraft.
